To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the asymptotic between-scale decorrelation properties of the DWT for a wide variety of stochastic processes can be described in a unified manner.

the covariance between wavelets coefficients associated with different wavelet scales decreases to zero as the wavelet filter width increases for a wide class Gaussian processes with a spectral density that is the product a fractional differencing spectral density and a bounded function.

(i) for stationary FD processes the covariance between wavelets associated with different scales is proportional to the scale difference to the power -2H, where H is the FD parameter, and (ii) the covariance between wavelett coefficients associated with different scale is asymptotically proportional to the scale differnce to the power -H, where H = 1/2, for nonstationary processes with a spectral density proportional to f-1/2.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a general theory that will provide a framework for establishing the asymptotic distribution theory of wavelet-based statistics for a wide class (including nonstationary) of stochastic processes.
the asymptotic properties of statistics based upon wavelet coefficients of stochastic processes.

the asymptotic properties of wavelet-based statistics, including the asymptotic covariance structure of wavelet coefficients, as the filter width used to form the wavelet transform is allowed to become arbitrarily wide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the asymptotic covariance properties of wavelets are well understood for many stochastic processes, and the results are useful for practical purposes.
the DWT is asymptotically uncorrelated for many stochastic processes of practical interest.

the between-scale covariance structure for wavelet coefficients is approximately zero for a large class of stochastic processes, and this approximation becomes better as the width of filter increases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DWT can be used for a wide class processes to approximate a multiresolution analysis (MRA) of the data.
we have shown that, under fairly mild assumptions, the wavelet transform is asymptotically uncorrelated for a large class of processes.

, under the conditions we impose, the wavelet coefficients of a process with a given SDF are approximately uncorrelated between scales, and the variances of the wavelet coefficients are approximately proportional to the power spectrum at the scale of interest.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for a wide class, of stochastic processes, the between-scale covariance between wavelet-based statistics is asymptotically negligible as the filter width used to form the wavelet coefficients increases.
the asymptotic theory is a useful guide for understanding the between-scale covariance structure of wavelet coefficients for a wide class and a variety of stochastic processes.
, in many cases, the asymptotic behavior of a wavelet-based statistic is driven by the asymptotic behavior in the between-scale covariance of the wavelet coefficients.
